runs.text: The most important finding is that liquidity is narrow and time-limited. At September 30, 2026 the Trust held cash of USD 40.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 650.0 million, together USD 690.1 million, and the revolver matures on June 29, 2027 with two six-month extensions subject to a fee and conditions; the company says it is exploring an extension or refinancing, with no replacement agreed. Fixed-rate maturities are USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028, so USD 1,586.9 million falls due before the end of 2028 against cash of USD 40.1 million. Availability of the revolver depends on collateral performance and covenant tests whose reported ratios are not in the pack. The mechanism is that a single secured facility supplies nearly all liquidity while the largest maturities arrive within the same window, so a failed or delayed refinancing would leave asset sales and new secured debt as the only sources. (Documentary Fact for the amounts and dates; Analyst Interpretation for the conclusion.) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities, Debt and capital structure]

The second finding is that leverage and cover are weak even after 2026 deleveraging. Principal debt of USD 4,652.3 million is 9.78x calculated last-twelve-month core EBITDA of USD 475.6 million (9.70x net of USD 40.1 million cash), down from 10.77x at FY2025, and core EBITDA covers last-twelve-month cash interest 1.41x, up from 1.35x. The Trust has a net loss of USD 463.7 million over the last twelve months, including USD 271.0 million of impairments, and operating cash flow less real estate improvements was negative USD 73.0 million. The EBITDA proxy includes earnings of hotels that have since been sold, so forward leverage on the retained portfolio is likely higher than shown. (Documentary Fact for reported amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the proxy and its direction, which is our inference and not a reported number.) [CP-1 Chart data, Financials and credit metrics, Calculations]

The third finding is that deleveraging depends on asset sales and equity that may not repeat. Debt fell by USD 852.5 million in nine months, funded by net equity proceeds of USD 541.8 million, new net lease mortgage notes, hotel and property sales and cash on hand. Each hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA, and further proceeds are subject to buyer demand; sales of eight hotels for USD 50.6 million closed after the quarter. The mechanism is that leverage improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.) [CP-1 Latest quarter and events; CP-1A Transaction summary]

The fourth finding is rent concentration. TravelCenters of America pays 68.2% of net lease annualized minimum rent under five master leases that expire in 2033, with rent coverage of 1.32x to 1.61x on those leases against 2.17x for the net lease portfolio, and BP Corporation North America guarantees the leases up to a cap of USD 2,782.9 million. Coverage is tenant-reported and unaudited, and the tenant's own financials are not in the pack. The leases expire one year after the 8.875% notes due 2032. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the timing link.) [CP-1A Company and operating model, Credit translations]

The fifth finding is covenant headroom in the indentures, which is adequate on the reported tests. Total debt to adjusted total assets is 53.9% against a 60% maximum, and income available for debt service to debt service is 1.83x against a 1.50x minimum, after being 58.7% and 1.59x at December 31, 2025. Holding debt constant, adjusted assets could fall by about 10.2% before the 60% test is reached, and income available for debt service could fall by about 18.0% before the 1.50x test is reached. Revolver covenants (minimum fixed charge coverage of 1.30x, collateral debt yield of 10%) have no reported figures, so their headroom is Not calculable. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivities, derived in Calculations.) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]

The sixth finding is subordination. Secured principal debt of USD 2,927.3 million is 62.9% of principal debt, up from 40.5% at December 31, 2025, because secured and equity capital replaced unsecured notes; USD 1,225.0 million of unsecured notes have no guarantees. No amendment, exchange or uptier of existing notes is documented, but unsecured creditors now sit behind more secured claims, which affects loss given default for them. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the implication.) [CP-1 Debt and capital structure; CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]

runs.text: Strengths. Deleveraging is real and documented: principal debt fell from USD 5,504.8 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 4,652.3 million at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Calculations]. Contractual rent is a stable core: net lease properties were 97.6% occupied with USD 395.5 million of annualized minimum rent and a 7.0 year weighted remaining term, which gives revenue visibility if tenants pay (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Indenture tests have headroom on all five reported measures at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]. All debt is fixed rate except the undrawn revolver, with an average annual coupon of 5.65% on current principal, so interest cost is not exposed to rates in the near term (Documentary Fact for the debt table; Analyst Interpretation for the exposure view) [CP-1 Calculations]. The manager bought shares in the April 2026 equity offering and distributions were held at a low level, which is documented supportive behaviour (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Retained hotels improved in the third quarter of 2026, with RevPAR up 8.3%, although the data is manager-reported and management attributes part of the gain to a weak 2025 comparison (Management Language, qualified) [CP-1A Company and operating model].

Weaknesses. Leverage is high and cover thin at 9.78x and 1.41x on our own EBITDA proxy, because the company reports no EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation) [CP-1 Chart data]. Liquidity depends on one secured revolver that expires June 29, 2027, and maturities of USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028 follow (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities]. Hotels are 74.7% of revenue with an operating expense ratio of 85.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and a segment loss after impairments, so earnings are operationally levered and volatile (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Calculations, Company and operating model]. Tenant concentration is high: one tenant is 68.2% of net lease rent and carries the lowest rent coverage among the top ten brands (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Earnings quality is poor: nine-month 2026 net loss was USD 463.0 million including USD 270.9 million of impairments (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The structure is secured-heavy and related-party dependent: the Trust has no employees, RMR manages it, and the Chair controls both the hotel operator Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, RMR's parent; terminating RMR without cause would require a fee based on 19 to 20 years of fees (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company profile, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Revolver covenant ratios, tenant financials, ratings and the investor presentation are absent (Insufficient Information; the missing items are listed in Gaps and the absence is not an adverse conclusion).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, buyout or sponsor transaction is present in the sources, so the transaction row for sponsor activity is Insufficient Information and not an adverse finding. The relevant transactions are financings and portfolio actions, all completed unless stated.

In September 2025 the Trust issued zero coupon senior secured notes due 2027 with 580,155 principal at maturity, raising net proceeds of approximately 490,000. The notes accrete at 7.50% per annum, are secured by first-priority liens on the equity of subsidiaries that own 36 travel centers, and have a one-time one-year extension option (10-K FY2025 page:196: "we issued $580,155 in aggregate principal amount at maturity of zero coupon senior secured notes due 2027"). On March 6, 2026 the Issuers, special purpose bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries, issued 745,000 of Series 2026-1 net lease mortgage notes in three classes with a 5.96% weighted coupon, maturing March 2031 (10-Q Q3 page:22: "issued $745,000 in aggregate principal amount of net lease mortgage notes in three classes"). The Trust contributed 158 properties to the collateral pool and the notes are non-recourse. The proceeds and cash on hand redeemed all 700,000 of the 8.375% senior guaranteed unsecured notes due 2029 with a make whole premium of 37,128. On April 2, 2026 the Trust sold 95,833,333 common shares at 6.00 per share after the reverse split, with net proceeds of approximately 541,798, which funded the redemption of the 450,000 5.50% guaranteed notes due 2027 and, with cash on hand, the 4.95% notes due 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:48). RMR, the manager, bought 8,333,333 shares in the offering at the public price (10-Q Q3 page:29). In September 2026 the 45,000 variable funding note was repaid and terminated using existing cash (10-Q Q3 page:23).

Liquidity effect, taken from the upstream debt and liquidity handoff: principal debt fell from 5,504,809 to 4,652,322 during the nine months, cash was 40,118 and the revolver was undrawn at 650,000 at September 30, 2026, but the revolver matures June 29, 2027. The Trust says it is exploring an extension or refinancing, and no replacement is agreed. The status of that exploration is pending and without assurance.

Portfolio transactions: in the nine months to September 30, 2026 the Trust sold 32 properties for 88,159, including six hotels in Q3 for 66,100, and acquired five net lease properties for 15,105 (10-Q Q3 pages:10 and 46). After the quarter, to November 2, 2026, it sold eight hotels with 1,509 keys for 50,600 and one net lease property for 295, acquired four net lease properties for 8,314, and agreed to sell one more net lease property for 655 subject to conditions. These are subsequent events and are not folded into September 30, 2026 figures. Eight of the ten exit hotels have therefore been sold and two remain for sale, which matches the 795 keys the filing says it is marketing; the retained set of 77 hotels is the earnings base going forward.

Related-party transaction in Q3 2026: in connection with a hotel sale, Sonesta waived an 11,035 termination fee in exchange for an extension of the management agreement for the remaining Sonesta retained hotels through June 30, 2043, and the Trust recorded the fee as an impairment loss (10-Q Q3 page:16). Creditor read: a cash fee was avoided, at the price of a longer commitment to an affiliated operator.
Use of proceeds is therefore stated and verifiable: debt retirement. No debt-funded distribution, dividend recapitalisation or asset drop-down to unrestricted subsidiaries is documented in the pack.

fields.value: Why the view is not READY: the pack holds filed statements and notes only. The evidence chain is statement or note text, then the risk that the credit agreement, indenture covenants and any management presentation are absent, then the consequence that covenant headroom on the revolver, adjusted EBITDA-type measures and management guidance cannot be established from the pack and must be logged as gaps rather than filled.

fields.value: Why the view is not CONDITIONAL: the Q3 report prints the debt note by class, the maturity table, the indenture covenant tests, liquidity and subsequent events, and the 10-K supplies the audited annual base. The method of each consumer can run on those pages with bounded gaps.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strongest contrary evidence: the committed revolving facility is the line the filing relies on for cash needs, and the filing says "We are currently exploring our options to extend or refinance our secured revolving credit facility." (Q3 10-Q, page:47). Its covenants and borrowing-base style conditions sit in a credit agreement that is not in the pack, so the consumers that size liquidity must carry that as a limitation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 10-K is the audited base. The auditor opinion begins "We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Service Properties Trust" (10-K, page:167). The cover gives the share count as "Number of the registrant’s common shares outstanding as of February 23, 2026: 168,061,029." (10-K, page:2). The balance sheet gives "168,070,129 and 166,636,537 shares issued and outstanding" (10-K, page:171). These are before the July 2026 reverse split. Schedule III is headed "(dollars in millions)" (10-K, page:213) while the notes to it say "NOTES TO SCHEDULE III December 31, 2025 (dollars in thousands)" (10-K, page:218). The unit label differs inside the same schedule and must be checked before any Schedule III figure is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All three are unaudited condensed statements and carry a three-month column (Q2 and Q3 also a year-to-date column). Q1 reports "168,054,570 and 168,070,129 shares issued and outstanding" (Q1 10-Q, page:2), which is unadjusted. Q2 reports "129,527,433 and 33,614,025 shares issued and outstanding" (Q2 10-Q, page:2), which is adjusted for the split. The Q3 10-Q states that share information is "retroactively adjusted for the 1-for-5 reverse share split" (Q3 10-Q, page:8) and its equity statement restates the March 31, 2026 balance as 33,610,914 shares (Q3 10-Q, page:3). The Q1 10-Q and the 10-K therefore cannot be combined with Q2 or Q3 share data without a split adjustment.

fields.value: The Q3 10-Q carries the full statement set. Balance sheet: "Cash and cash equivalents 40,118 346,813" for September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (page:2). Income statement: "Net loss (87,940) (46,945) (462,956) (201,539)" for the three and nine months of 2026 and 2025 (page:3). Cash flow: "Cash paid for interest $ 196,080 $ 239,155" for the nine months (page:5). Segment note: "Segment profit (loss) 36,414 (52,142) (15,728) 47,206 6,909 54,115" for the three months, net lease then hotels then total (page:31). All amounts are in USD thousands.

fields.value: Debt note: "Our principal debt obligations at September 30, 2026 were: (1) $1,725,000 aggregate outstanding principal amount of senior unsecured notes" (page:20), with senior secured notes and net lease mortgage notes also stated there. The mortgage note table closes with "Total / weighted average $ 1,347,167 5.80%" (page:22). A per-instrument carrying value and fair value table is on page:33. The maturity table totals "$ 4,652,322" (page:49). Revolver: "we had no amounts outstanding under our revolving credit facility and $650,000 available for borrowing" (page:20), and "The maturity date of our revolving credit facility is June 29, 2027" (page:20). The indenture tests are printed, for example "Total debt / adjusted total assets 53.9% Maximum of 60%" and "Consolidated income available for debt service / debt service 1.83x Minimum of 1.50x" (page:51). The guarantee perimeter is stated: "Our $1,225,000 of senior unsecured notes do not have the benefit of any guarantees." (page:53).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The three EX-99.1 files are one-page announcements. Each says the results "can be found at the Quarterly Results section of SVC’s website" (Q3 release, page:1; the same wording is on page:1 of the Q1 and Q2 releases). They contain no income statement, balance sheet, adjusted measure, reconciliation or guidance. The Q3 release adds "SVC also posted an updated investor presentation to its website." (page:1) but the presentation is not in the pack, so its content cannot be used and nothing in this review relies on it. The releases do give portfolio counts, for example "87 hotels with approximately 20,000 guest rooms" at September 30, 2026 (Q3 release, page:1). They are management statements and are subordinate to the filed 10-Q, which reports 87 hotels at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q, page:7).

fields.value: No conflict between sources was found in the items checked. The one difference noted is a unit label, not a conflicting figure: the Schedule III heading in millions against its notes in thousands (10-K, page:213 and page:218). Its downstream effect falls on any consumer that uses Schedule III property data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The three 10-Qs are separate active periodic reports for consecutive quarters, and the 10-K is the annual report. None supersedes another. The Q3 10-Q supersedes the earlier 10-Qs only for facts stated as of September 30, 2026. Prior-period comparatives inside later filings are retained as stated there; this module does not rule which version controls a given fact.

fields.value: For the HTML Model objective the pack holds: discrete three-month columns for each of Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 and the 2025 comparatives; year-to-date columns in the Q2 and Q3 reports; FY2025 and FY2024 annual statements in the 10-K; a segment note for net lease and hotels; debt by class with carrying and fair values; and cash paid for interest and income taxes (Q3 10-Q, page:5 and the supplemental table after it). Source evidence is sufficient for these. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This module does not assert normalised quarters, reconciliation or downstream input acceptance. A last-twelve-month view and Q4 2025 are not printed as such and would have to be derived downstream from filed columns; that derivation is not performed here.

fields.value: The reported financial base is complete enough for the requested use, with limits. Four filings give full statements, a debt note by class, a maturity table, the senior notes indenture tests, revolver availability and subsequent events through November 2, 2026. The company prints no EBITDA, so the leverage and cover charts use a core EBITDA defined and calculated here from statement lines: total revenues less hotel operating expenses, net lease operating expenses, general and administrative expenses and transaction related costs. Principal debt fell by 852,487 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, funded by net equity proceeds of 541,798, new net lease mortgage notes, asset sales and cash on hand. Gross leverage on LTM core EBITDA moved from 10.77x at FY2025 to 9.78x at the third quarter of 2026, and cash interest cover from 1.35x to 1.41x. Both are weak, and the LTM EBITDA still includes earnings of hotels that have since been sold, so forward leverage on the retained portfolio is likely worse than the LTM figure shows; that last point is analyst inference, not a reported number. Liquidity is thin in cash and rests on a single undrawn secured revolver that matures within nine months. The balance sheet is secured-heavy: secured principal of 2,927,322 is 63% of principal debt, a share calculated in the Calculations section.

fields.value: Leverage. Evidence: principal debt of 4,652,322 and calculated LTM core EBITDA of 475,642 give 9.78x, down from 10.77x at FY2025. Mechanism: the improvement comes mostly from the numerator, as 852,487 of debt was retired using equity and sale proceeds, while LTM EBITDA fell from 511,334 as hotels were sold and hotel revenue dropped. Implication: deleveraging is real but asset-sale driven, so each further hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA and the ratio improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. The hotel segment lost 272,673 in the nine months of 2026 after impairments (10-Q Q3 page:31), so the retained hotels are not yet self-supporting after impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage. Evidence: LTM cash interest of 336,491 against core EBITDA of 475,642 gives 1.41x, and the fixed-rate table shows annual interest of 263,082 on the current debt (10-Q Q3 page:62). Mechanism: LTM cash interest still includes interest on notes repaid during 2026, while LTM EBITDA includes earnings of sold hotels. Implication: cover on the current debt is likely above 1.41x on a run-rate basis only if EBITDA holds, which the hotel sales make uncertain. The 2027 zero coupon notes add no cash interest but accrete at 7.50% per annum, so the cash coverage metric understates the claim growing until maturity.

fields.value: Liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash of 40,118, an undrawn 650,000 revolver maturing June 29, 2027, maturities of 584,150 in 2027 and 1,002,775 in 2028, and the stated search for a revolver extension or refinancing. Mechanism: the revolver is secured on 55 properties and its availability depends on collateral performance, value and covenants, including a fixed charge coverage minimum of 1.30x that the pack does not report against. Implication: the 2027 wall (revolver expiry and the zero coupon notes) is the near-term pressure point. The two six-month extension options require a fee and a 1.50x fixed charge coverage ratio for the first extension, a test the pack gives no figure for.

Mechanism: unsecured and unguaranteed creditors sit behind secured claims on the best assets and behind subsidiary-level claims. Implication: recovery for the 1,225,000 of unguaranteed unsecured notes depends on residual value after secured claims; the indenture test of unencumbered assets to unsecured debt at 273.2% shows asset cover on the company's definition but is not a recovery estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a two-engine REIT with different risk profiles. About a quarter of revenue is contractual rent from service-focused retail net lease properties, and the rest is hotel operating revenue where the Trust carries the operating cost and pays managers. The net lease engine is concentrated: one tenant, TravelCenters of America, accounts for 68.2% of annualized minimum rent through five master leases that expire in 2033, with a limited BP guaranty and rent coverage on those leases of 1.32x to 1.61x, against 2.17x for the whole net lease portfolio and at least 2.18x for every other top ten brand. The hotel engine is being shrunk: 112 hotels were sold in 2025, more in 2026, and 53 Sonesta managed hotels plus 17 Hyatt and seven Radisson hotels are the stated retained set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Trust is externally managed. It has no employees, RMR provides all personnel, and the Chair, who is also a Managing Trustee, controls Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, the parent of RMR. That makes three related-party strands, manager, hotel operator and equity investee, which sit on both sides of fee, capital spending and asset-sale decisions. Documented behaviour in 2026 was supportive of creditors: the manager joined the equity offering, distributions were held at 0.05 per share per quarter, and the proceeds retired 1,550,000 of unsecured notes, and cash retired a 45,000 variable funding note. The same year raised the secured share of principal debt, which moves claim ranking against unsecured noteholders, although it was done through new, disclosed financings and not by amending existing notes; no non-pro-rata exchange, uptier or drop-down of existing noteholders is documented in the pack.

fields.value: In September 2025 the Trust issued zero coupon senior secured notes due 2027 with 580,155 principal at maturity, raising net proceeds of approximately 490,000. The notes accrete at 7.50% per annum, are secured by first-priority liens on the equity of subsidiaries that own 36 travel centers, and have a one-time one-year extension option (10-K FY2025 page:196: "we issued $580,155 in aggregate principal amount at maturity of zero coupon senior secured notes due 2027"). On March 6, 2026 the Issuers, special purpose bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries, issued 745,000 of Series 2026-1 net lease mortgage notes in three classes with a 5.96% weighted coupon, maturing March 2031 (10-Q Q3 page:22: "issued $745,000 in aggregate principal amount of net lease mortgage notes in three classes"). The Trust contributed 158 properties to the collateral pool and the notes are non-recourse. The proceeds and cash on hand redeemed all 700,000 of the 8.375% senior guaranteed unsecured notes due 2029 with a make whole premium of 37,128. On April 2, 2026 the Trust sold 95,833,333 common shares at 6.00 per share after the reverse split, with net proceeds of approximately 541,798, which funded the redemption of the 450,000 5.50% guaranteed notes due 2027 and, with cash on hand, the 4.95% notes due 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:48). RMR, the manager, bought 8,333,333 shares in the offering at the public price (10-Q Q3 page:29). In September 2026 the 45,000 variable funding note was repaid and terminated using existing cash (10-Q Q3 page:23).

The Trust says it is exploring an extension or refinancing, and no replacement is agreed. The status of that exploration is pending and without assurance.

After the quarter, to November 2, 2026, it sold eight hotels with 1,509 keys for 50,600 and one net lease property for 295, acquired four net lease properties for 8,314, and agreed to sell one more net lease property for 655 subject to conditions. These are subsequent events and are not folded into September 30, 2026 figures. Eight of the ten exit hotels have therefore been sold and two remain for sale, which matches the 795 keys the filing says it is marketing; the retained set of 77 hotels is the earnings base going forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability. Evidence: net lease rental income of 101,141 in Q3 2026 is 25.3% of revenue, and 68.2% of annualized minimum rent is TA. Risk mechanic: contractual rent is stable while the tenant pays, but one tenant, on leases with the lowest portfolio coverage, makes the rent stream effectively a single credit with a BP guaranty capped at 2,782,917. Credit implication: debt service from rent is supported but concentrated; a TA payment problem would affect more than two thirds of net lease rent, and the 2033 expiry sits one year after the 2032 notes mature. A counter: portfolio rent coverage is 2.17x on tenant-reported data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: hotel operating expenses were 85.7% of hotel revenue in Q3 2026 and the hotel segment lost 52,142 after impairments. Risk mechanic: the Trust carries hotel cost and pays fee layers ahead of its own return, so a revenue decline cuts margin more than revenue. Credit implication: hotel cash flow is the swing factor for cover; improving RevPAR on retained hotels helps, but 74.7% of revenue still comes from hotels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration and related-party risk. Evidence: Sonesta manages 62 hotels, about 39.9% of total historical real estate investments, and is controlled by the Chair; RMR runs the Trust with no employees. Risk mechanic: fees, capital spending and sale decisions are negotiated between related parties. Credit implication: monitoring of related-party flows is a standing requirement; the Q3 fee waiver for a longer term shows the trade-offs.

fields.value: Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor exists, RMR bought shares in the offering, distributions were held at a low level. Risk mechanic: manager fees are asset and return based, not leverage based. Credit implication: alignment is moderate; support is modest in size and not a commitment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Service Properties Trust is a highly leveraged, thinly covered REIT whose credit is improving through asset sales and 2026 equity, but it still depends on one tenant and on refinancing a revolver that expires on June 29, 2027. The strongest support is deleveraging: principal debt fell USD 852.5 million to USD 4,652.3 million, indenture tests have headroom, and net lease rent is contractual with 97.6% occupancy. The weakest point is liquidity of USD 690.1 million, nearly all an undrawn secured revolver, against USD 1,586.9 million of maturities in 2027 and 2028 and cash interest cover of 1.41x. The outcome turns on the revolver extension or refinancing, the pace and price of hotel sales, and TravelCenters of America continuing to pay rent. [CP-1 Debt and capital structure, Liquidity, Covenants; CP-1A Business and transaction view]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Service Properties Trust is a deleveraging, hotel-to-net-lease transition credit whose debt service is supported by concentrated contractual rent but whose near-term outcome depends on refinancing the 2027 revolver and executing hotel sales on acceptable terms. (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Financial base view and CP-1A Business and transaction view.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most important finding is that liquidity is narrow and time-limited. At September 30, 2026 the Trust held cash of USD 40.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 650.0 million, together USD 690.1 million, and the revolver matures on June 29, 2027 with two six-month extensions subject to a fee and conditions; the company says it is exploring an extension or refinancing, with no replacement agreed. Fixed-rate maturities are USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028, so USD 1,586.9 million falls due before the end of 2028 against cash of USD 40.1 million. Availability of the revolver depends on collateral performance and covenant tests whose reported ratios are not in the pack. The mechanism is that a single secured facility supplies nearly all liquidity while the largest maturities arrive within the same window, so a failed or delayed refinancing would leave asset sales and new secured debt as the only sources. (Documentary Fact for the amounts and dates; Analyst Interpretation for the conclusion.) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities, Debt and capital structure]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second finding is that leverage and cover are weak even after 2026 deleveraging. Principal debt of USD 4,652.3 million is 9.78x calculated last-twelve-month core EBITDA of USD 475.6 million (9.70x net of USD 40.1 million cash), down from 10.77x at FY2025, and core EBITDA covers last-twelve-month cash interest 1.41x, up from 1.35x. The Trust has a net loss of USD 463.7 million over the last twelve months, including USD 271.0 million of impairments, and operating cash flow less real estate improvements was negative USD 73.0 million. The EBITDA proxy includes earnings of hotels that have since been sold, so forward leverage on the retained portfolio is likely higher than shown. (Documentary Fact for reported amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the proxy and its direction, which is our inference and not a reported number.) [CP-1 Chart data, Financials and credit metrics, Calculations]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third finding is that deleveraging depends on asset sales and equity that may not repeat. Debt fell by USD 852.5 million in nine months, funded by net equity proceeds of USD 541.8 million, new net lease mortgage notes, hotel and property sales and cash on hand. Each hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA, and further proceeds are subject to buyer demand; sales of eight hotels for USD 50.6 million closed after the quarter. The mechanism is that leverage improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.) [CP-1 Latest quarter and events; CP-1A Transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth finding is rent concentration. TravelCenters of America pays 68.2% of net lease annualized minimum rent under five master leases that expire in 2033, with rent coverage of 1.32x to 1.61x on those leases against 2.17x for the net lease portfolio, and BP Corporation North America guarantees the leases up to a cap of USD 2,782.9 million. Coverage is tenant-reported and unaudited, and the tenant's own financials are not in the pack. The leases expire one year after the 8.875% notes due 2032. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the timing link.) [CP-1A Company and operating model, Credit translations]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth finding is covenant headroom in the indentures, which is adequate on the reported tests. Total debt to adjusted total assets is 53.9% against a 60% maximum, and income available for debt service to debt service is 1.83x against a 1.50x minimum, after being 58.7% and 1.59x at December 31, 2025. Holding debt constant, adjusted assets could fall by about 10.2% before the 60% test is reached, and income available for debt service could fall by about 18.0% before the 1.50x test is reached. Revolver covenants (minimum fixed charge coverage of 1.30x, collateral debt yield of 10%) have no reported figures, so their headroom is Not calculable. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivities, derived in Calculations.) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sixth finding is subordination. Secured principal debt of USD 2,927.3 million is 62.9% of principal debt, up from 40.5% at December 31, 2025, because secured and equity capital replaced unsecured notes; USD 1,225.0 million of unsecured notes have no guarantees. No amendment, exchange or uptier of existing notes is documented, but unsecured creditors now sit behind more secured claims, which affects loss given default for them. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the implication.) [CP-1 Debt and capital structure; CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Deleveraging is real and documented: principal debt fell from USD 5,504.8 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 4,652.3 million at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Calculations]. Contractual rent is a stable core: net lease properties were 97.6% occupied with USD 395.5 million of annualized minimum rent and a 7.0 year weighted remaining term, which gives revenue visibility if tenants pay (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Indenture tests have headroom on all five reported measures at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]. All debt is fixed rate except the undrawn revolver, with an average annual coupon of 5.65% on current principal, so interest cost is not exposed to rates in the near term (Documentary Fact for the debt table; Analyst Interpretation for the exposure view) [CP-1 Calculations]. The manager bought shares in the April 2026 equity offering and distributions were held at a low level, which is documented supportive behaviour (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Retained hotels improved in the third quarter of 2026, with RevPAR up 8.3%, although the data is manager-reported and management attributes part of the gain to a weak 2025 comparison (Management Language, qualified) [CP-1A Company and operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage is high and cover thin at 9.78x and 1.41x on our own EBITDA proxy, because the company reports no EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation) [CP-1 Chart data]. Liquidity depends on one secured revolver that expires June 29, 2027, and maturities of USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028 follow (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities]. Hotels are 74.7% of revenue with an operating expense ratio of 85.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and a segment loss after impairments, so earnings are operationally levered and volatile (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Calculations, Company and operating model]. Tenant concentration is high: one tenant is 68.2% of net lease rent and carries the lowest rent coverage among the top ten brands (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Earnings quality is poor: nine-month 2026 net loss was USD 463.0 million including USD 270.9 million of impairments (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The structure is secured-heavy and related-party dependent: the Trust has no employees, RMR manages it, and the Chair controls both the hotel operator Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, RMR's parent; terminating RMR without cause would require a fee based on 19 to 20 years of fees (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company profile, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Revolver covenant ratios, tenant financials, ratings and the investor presentation are absent (Insufficient Information; the missing items are listed in Gaps and the absence is not an adverse conclusion).
